item.title: Re: Nothing is new under the sun.
item.content:encoded:
Basically my point is, nothing is new. Everything has been done.

Apologies for the necropost, but I have to point out that this is what you call a "thought terminating cliche", and a rather foolish and nihilistic one at that. Everything has not been done, and new things are created every day. While we as humans rely on tropes and archetypes to convey meaning, they are tools and shorthand, not limitations- and we can create new ones.

Take music, for instance- imagine if everyone just accepted the idea that classical was the ultimate culmination of music, and gave up trying anything but endless imitation of a single style, never tried anything new and dangerous. Think about it: No Jazz. No Blues. No Techno. No Heavy Metal, Lounge, or Pop. No Ragtime, Accapella, or Dubstep. No Soul, Gangster Rap, or Swing. A world of stagnant dead music endlessly parroting a single proscribed method.

Never buy into the garbage about creativity being dead. There are endless forms most beautiful to explore.

item.title: Nothing is new under the sun.
item.content:encoded:
I will say this. There is a fine line between what can be considered a cliche and what can be considered a genre. I don't exactly know what can be what on this list but I do know that with so many SCPs out there it is not easy to avoid a lot of what is on that list. I do believe that a lot of the stuff here is still doable. And I am seeing numerous claims to the fact that this particular form of writing or any one particular cliche is very 'difficult.' I mean, come on, to create anything is very difficult it just depends on how much effort one puts into the work and the only real issue that I am frequently seeing in low rated SCPs is the obvious amount of time that was put into the work (or lack thereof) 'cliche' or not.

Basically my point is, nothing is new. Everything has been done. The key to creating anything unique (not just SCPs) is not coming up with a completely and totally original concept (because that really is all but impossible at this point) but taking a concept that appeals to you and putting forth the time and effort into putting your own spin on it.

item.title: A Few Things
item.content:encoded:
Soulless already covered Uncontainable, so I'll just add that there's a huge difference between Uncontainable and Uncontained. There's nothing wrong with an SCP the Foundation hasn't managed to contain yet, so long as it's clear there's still the effort to find a way.

On the note of pretty pplz, and catering to their whim: I see a tendency to go the other way, and that's just as big a mistake. If a humanoid SCP asks for a set of books to pass the time, and they've been otherwise behaving themselves, there's no reason not to provide it to them. Rewarding good behavior gives them an incentive to cooperate, as well as something for the Foundation to take away. Generally, ask yourself: Could someone in a maximum security prison reasonably expect to get it? Then there's no reason to deny it to a humanoid SCP. The only times to refuse such a request is when it takes up excessive resources, breaches security in some fashion, or the SCP in question has been uncooperative.

Finally, Spherical and Cubical objects: Please note the difference between something that's a sphere or a cube because the author couldn't think of an item, and something that's a sphere or a cube because that's what that object would reasonably be expected to be. If an SCP is a basketball, then it's going to be a sphere. If it's a six-sided die, it's going to be a cube. Similarly, SCP-1947 is a sphere because a space probe would reasonably be a sphere. Generally, if there's more to the description beyond sphere or cube of X substance (or, god help us all, of [DATA EXPUNGED]), it's probably all right.

These are some of the biggest misunderstandings I see when people attempt to use the list of Cliches, and I think it would be helpful if your guide addressed them. That being said, good job in working to clarify the Cliches list and make it more useful.
